name: Spiss
kurzbeschreibung: Highest-altitude settlement in the district of Landeck, near the Swiss border, offering solitude and breathtaking mountain scenery.
beschreibung:
Spiss lies at an elevation of 1,740 meters in the district of Landeck, not far from the Swiss border at the entrance to the Samnauntal – and is thus the highest permanently inhabited settlement in the district. The hamlet with its roughly 100 inhabitants nestles on a sun-exposed high plateau between the Gribellekopf and the Pezinerspitz, with an open view toward Engadin and Silvretta. Anyone who comes here leaves the bustle of the Inntal far behind: the narrow road winds steeply up from Pfunds, and once you arrive at the top, one thing above all is noticeable – silence.

Hiking is the main thing in Spiss. The village is a starting point for tours into the surrounding mountain world, for example to the Frudigerjochhütte or up toward the Gribellekopf, where you stand at 2,500 meters among chamois and alpine roses. In winter, the cross-country ski trail runs from here into Swiss Samnaun, and ski tourers use the untouched slopes around the village. Particularly characteristic is the location at the tri-border area Österreich–Schweiz–Italien, which has always made Spiss, despite its remoteness, a small hub of alpine transit routes.

When it comes to food, Spiss offers honest Tiroler fare – Graukasnocken and Kaspressknödel in simple inns, often with products from the surrounding farms' own livestock operations. Anyone seeking absolute quiet, far from well-trodden tourism paths, is in the right place here. 🌲
text:
Overview

Spiss is situated at an elevation of 1,627 meters in the far southwest of Tyrol in the Landeck district, perched on the sunny southern slopes of the Samnaun Alps high above the Spiss gorge and the Schergenbach stream, which delineates the Swiss border. Home to around 100 residents, this peaceful village is officially the highest political municipality in Austria and the smallest in the Landeck district. Spiss is celebrated for its pristine high-alpine environment, authentic mountain farming heritage, and profound tranquility. Due to its immediate proximity to the Swiss duty-free enclave of Samnaun, Spiss combines untouched solitude with seamless access to premier shopping and the expansive cross-border Silvretta Arena ski resort.

History

The high-altitude territory was cleared and settled in the High Middle Ages by Romansh pioneers from the Swiss Engadin and Samnaun valleys. The village name originates from the Latin-Romansh spissus, signifying dense thicket or scrubland. The settlements of Unterspiss and Gstalda were first documented in 1302, with Oberspiss recorded in 1318. Historically governed under the Nauders court, Spiss gained municipal autonomy in 1547. Due to the precipitous gorge, the community was often cut off from North Tyrol for months each winter, maintaining economic ties almost exclusively via packhorse trails into Switzerland. A safe, year-round road entirely on Austrian soil was established only in 1980 with the construction of the Spisser Landesstraße, heavily protected by avalanche galleries and tunnels. The late Baroque church dedicated to Saint John the Baptist was built in 1777/1778.

Getting there

Reaching Spiss involves a scenic mountain drive. Motorists travel along the A12 Inntal motorway or S16 expressway to the Landeck junction, following the B180 Reschen highway through Ried and Pfunds to Kajetansbrücke, where the L348 Spisser road climbs dramatically through the gorge with avalanche shelters and the Anna Tunnel (winter equipment essential). The road continues across the Swiss border directly into Samnaun. Train travelers arrive at the Landeck-Zams international railway station on the Arlberg mainline. From there, regional VVT buses run via Pfunds to Spiss, with cross-border PostAuto connections continuing into Samnaun.

Tips

A major attraction is duty-free shopping in the Swiss tax-free enclave of Samnaun, located just minutes away, offering perfume, luxury goods, and fuel across 40 specialized stores (customs allowances apply). Skiers can board the famous double-decker Twinliner cable car in Samnaun-Ravaisch to access the Silvretta Arena Ischgl-Samnaun, boasting 239 kilometers of snow-assured pistes. During summer, hike the historic Smugglers' Trail over the Zanders meadows and Fliesser Alm into Switzerland, or ascend scenic summits such as Mount Gribellekopf (2,892 m) for breathtaking vistas across the Eastern Alps.
